key_insight: Instead of assigning discrete tokens to spatial patches, Channel-wise Vector Quantization (CVQ) quantizes each feature-map channel, turning an image into discrete levels of visual detail and enabling autoregressive "next-channel" prediction.
problem_solved: Patch-wise tokenization is spatially coarse and can blur fine-grained visual detail; CVQ addresses this by providing a channel-level discrete representation that better captures per-feature detail and supports new autoregressive modeling schemes.
method: Channel-wise quantization: apply vector quantization independently to each channel of a feature map, producing channel-level discrete codes.
Reframe tokenization: represent images as sequences of channel tokens (discrete levels of visual detail) rather than a grid of patch tokens.
Autoregressive modeling: build a visual autoregressive framework that predicts the next channel token (next-channel prediction) to generate or compress images.
impact: CVQ offers a finer-grained, semantically meaningful tokenization that can improve generative modeling, compression, and representation learning workflows by enabling channel-wise autoregressive strategies and potentially more compact or informative tokens.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram comparing patch-wise tokenization (patch grid → tokens) vs. channel-wise tokenization (per-channel quantization → token levels).
Pipeline flowchart: image → backbone features → CVQ (per-channel codebook lookup) → channel-token sequence → autoregressive next-channel predictor.
Per-channel visualization: a set of channel heatmaps before and after quantization to show discrete levels of detail.
Sequence diagram illustrating next-channel prediction steps during autoregressive generation/compression.
